name: Rich rendering: markdown, code, math, Mermaid, diffs
gap: Shipped for assistant turns only; human turns are plain text; no diff message type.
strengths: ChatMarkdown already covers code, media and charts for agent output; keep it as the single renderer.

name: Typing indicators (including agents)
gap: Delivered by 6 s polling, not push; agents are not shown as typers (agent progress is via run stream).
strengths: Throttled 3 s beat, 8 s decay, caller writes only own row, no content in rows: keep.

name: Stop a running agent turn
gap: No bare-'stop' text intercept (minor).
strengths: Stop aborts SSE then records cancelled in Session Core, distinguishing recorded vs local-only stops: keep.

name: Room roster and member management UI
gap: Minor: the role at add time is fixed to editor (see C-t1-02-007), and members and agents live in cockpit tabs rather than a side pane.
strengths: Roster comes straight from Control; agents are Control service subjects; an authorized agent without a published identity is shown honestly; managed_subject_types stops a human roster edit from removing agents; the owne…

name: Agent memory recall and search
gap: Not covered by a baseline record; save_memory/recall_memory tools exist in execution-core (grep in this step). Whether Space room turns offer them and how memory is scoped per Space (audience labels) is unverified.
strengths: Per the reference record, Verevon's learned memory (semantic retrieval, Dreaming) is richer than qm's notebook; keep it. Worth borrowing: recall deltas to save tokens and per-scope audience labels.

name: Skills invoked from a / picker in the composer
strengths: Verevon is ahead of qm: lazily loaded catalogue, keyboard picker shared with @, org/personal scope badges on chips, sent as structured skill_ids resolved server-side in Model Gateway rather than as inserted text. Keep t…

name: Surface plugins isolated from core (signed-HTTP boundary)
strengths: Verevon's plane architecture (no cross-plane DB access, Frontend gateway as BFF, Model proposes / Quarry executes) is an equal or stronger version of this boundary. Keep it, and make future Channel Plane adapters follow…

name: Agent as a first-class, labelled room member (own identity, owner provenance, profile)
gap: No visible 'managed by <owner>' on agent posts, no agent profile page (what it can read/do, skills, model, cost), and the avatar colour chosen at creation is never rendered (SpaceAgent has no colour field).
strengths: Agents are Control service subjects on the same roster as people, joined Control-first; the UI honestly shows the third state 'access granted, identity not published'; turn attribution (author subject, agent persona) is…

name: Agent authority model: whose authority an agent carries in a room
gap: No explicit turn-origin enum on decisions (direct vs ambient vs automation); revocation fan-out to the Model Plane is plain NATS, best effort (tolerates loss); no negative test list pinning human-only decisions.
strengths: Agents are their own Control service subjects; Control-signed, short-lived, effect-bound decisions; Space access never widens an owner-plane ACL; registry visibility explicitly does not grant authority. Ahead of QM's ac…

name: Layered instruction hierarchy (org, room, agent) with history
gap: No versioning/history of Space instructions.
strengths: Platform > org > Space > user > agent hierarchy is shipped; client-supplied values stripped; server-composed. Equal or ahead of QM.

name: Human review queue for agent-drafted replies
gap: Shipped in the support Inbox (outside Spaces): persisted drafts, a draft lease for concurrent editors and AI reply suggestions/proposals. Not available for agent drafts inside a Space.
strengths: Verevon's per-conversation draft lease (claim/release) is stronger than QM's conflict detection for multi-human editing; keep it and generalize it to Space-shared drafts (already a baseline open item).

name: Single transport-neutral admission pipeline with ordered side effects
gap: No baseline record in this category; from the backend baseline (SRC), every room post goes browser -> gateway -> Control thread decision -> Model Gateway -> Session Core, and agents use the same decision path. A human-o…
strengths: Control-issued, content-bound decisions are one authority chokepoint for humans and agents; keep any new transport (push, CLI, external channel) behind it.

name: Encryption posture: server-managed chat, no E2EE for messages, selective owner-private encryption
gap: No E2EE (same as all references for chat). Customer-managed keys not checked.
strengths: Verevon's Zero-Data-Retention propagation (typed ZDR refusals end to end) goes beyond every reference's posture; keep ZDR as a hard constraint on any new push/cache tier.

name: Membership-versioned writes that fence stale rosters
gap: No baseline record in this category; backend baseline (SRC) shows Control decisions bind audience ref/hash/revision and authority revision and Session Core verifies them.
strengths: Signed, short-lived decisions bound to audience revision and payload digest are stronger than QM's in-process roster version; keep.

name: Server-resolved tenant binding and multi-tenant isolation
gap: No type-level admission token or DB write fence equivalent recorded; isolation rests on gateway/Convex re-checks (not verified that every Convex table carries tenant-leading indexes).
strengths: Org derived from the verified session, membership re-checked per call, 12 forged authority fields stripped at the BFF, approvals keyed by JWT org. Keep the fail-closed re-check and strip list.

name: AI data boundary and AI-interaction governance
gap: Shared-read gate exists server-side but the timeline swallows the 403 (v-space-ui-097 partial); no admin switch catalogue for AI capabilities was recorded.
strengths: Immutable audience snapshots (set + hash + revision) bound into signed decisions, and the architectural rule that Space access never widens an owner-plane ACL, are stronger and more verifiable than the incumbents' polic…

name: Human-only authority walls and approval provenance on every agent request
gap: Retirement of standing grants and an explicit 'standing vs one-off approval' label on each room effect were not recorded.
strengths: Ed25519-signed, short-lived Control decisions bind subject, org, Space, audience, authority revision, privacy policy, action, schema hash, payload digest and idempotency key; deny-by-default effect policies. This exceed…

name: Accessibility: screen readers, keyboard regions, reduced motion, high contrast
gap: Small gaps: no forced-colors/high-contrast rules and no F6-style region cycling were found.
strengths: aria-live rows for streaming agent activity, colour-independent status marks, roving-focus tablist and reduced-motion queries: at or above buzz/qm level for the Space surface.

name: Thin client behind a server-side identity holder (BFF, no tokens in the browser)
strengths: Rust gateway is a same-origin BFF for all Space routes; the browser holds no upstream credential. Equal to qm and stronger than Electron shells that hold tokens locally.

name: One event log, several lenses (fast chat, slow decisions/approvals, automation traces) and per-surface projections
gap: No per-lens notification defaults and no external-surface presenters (Channel Plane docs-only).
strengths: Activity tab already reads five owner sources through one salience-ordered grammar with lenses (Everything, Needs attention, Work and effects, Conversations, Authority) next to the Chat lens, and the BFF stays a proxy. …

name: Empty states, zero states and suggested starters
gap: Room intro offers Start a conversation and Create an agent; no add-people/add-knowledge cards, no suggested starters, no coachmarks.
strengths: Every tab distinguishes nothing / could-not-load / not-published, which is stricter than the references. Keep; optionally add "fill a draft" starters and an add-people card.

name: Honest-state UX: unknown is not zero, never silently stuck, facts decide (not timers)
gap: One known exception: the timeline hides a 403 space_read_not_authorized behind preview text (SpaceRoomTimeline.tsx:201), i.e. a silent refusal. No typed resume-point failure taxonomy for agent runs in the room.
strengths: Server-composed unavailable[] {section, code, reason} contract and "gap, not empty" rendering are equal to Buzz's rules and are enforced in code (Buzz's are DOC). Keep and extend to every new chip, count and pane.

name: Calm destructive confirmation (arm-in-place, explicit kept-vs-lost)
gap: Kept-vs-lost wording could be made explicit for agent revoke and member removal.
strengths: SpaceConfirmButton arms in place and disarms after 6 s or on blur; personal-Space deletion shows per-plane receipts, which is stronger than the reference. Keep.
